scope: Direct shared scanEdit Split on the three original PLY scans with one manufactured finite planar triangle cutter per scan. These runs did not use a browser worker or QuickSurface.
candidate: Uncommitted combined working tree based on b6fcef2c6e99e0bc61c96ae3b9fb512be951ab02; not the published PR head.
method: The opt-in scan-split-single-mesh-original-local test loads each PLY with its original indexed topology, constructs a finite cutter at the X midpoint, calls runScanEdit with sourceIndexed, checks a nonempty cut and indexed/expanded agreement, compares input/output area within 1e-6 relative, and verifies source position, indexed vertex and triangle digests are unchanged. Runs are sequential under the 4 GiB owned-job limit.
workerDispatcher: The actual processing-worker dispatcher was invoked in a test harness with structuredClone and its declared transfer list. The first scan passed with a 684920832-byte recorded job peak; m2-worker-original-ply1-20261028-r1-guard.json. The third scan passed indexed/expanded agreement, area and source preservation with a 4295151616-byte recorded job peak; m2-worker-original-ply3-20261028-r1-guard.json. The configured job limit was 4294967296 bytes; the reported peak is 184320 bytes higher, so no usable headroom is demonstrated. This in-process harness includes a structured-clone copy and does not measure a real browser's process distribution. The second scan was not tested through this dispatcher.
limitations: The first test attempt assumed every scan would yield exactly two components and failed for ply-1. The check was corrected to require more than one and record the actual count; it does not establish the original component count or expected native component count.
The retained source digests do not include the cutter. Area and indexed agreement alone do not prove exact seam placement or native equivalence.
These direct operation runs do not establish browser-worker transfer, rendered GUI/public-MCP behavior, save/reopen, cancellation, or the full native comparison on these inputs.
